title: Bread Lines
speaker: treasury
body: {speaker} reports queues for bread and soup stretching around the block in {town}. Factories are laying off by the hundred and the tax receipts are falling with them.

options.label: Launch public works
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.5 months of GDP · satisfaction +6 · grievance −10 · a reformist deed

options.label: Open soup kitchens
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.2 months of GDP · grievance −5 · relief remembered abroad

title: The Contractors' Bills
speaker: treasury
body: The new roads and dams are rising, but {speaker} lays the invoices on the desk. Some contractors are plainly padding their costs, and the opposition has noticed.

options.label: Pay and press on
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · satisfaction +3 · legitimacy −3

title: The Union Question
speaker: interior
body: {speaker} says the workers of {town} have formed unions of their own accord and want them recognised in law. The mill owners want them broken.

title: The Union Congress
speaker: interior
body: The unions have federated, and their first congress threatens a general strike unless a minimum wage is set. {speaker} says they mean it.

options.label: Legislate a minimum wage
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · grievance −10 · satisfaction +5

options.label: Call their bluff
options.tooltip: Grievance +12 · legitimacy −5 · a crackdown if it comes to blows

title: Agitators in the Foundries
speaker: interior
body: {speaker} brings pamphlets seized in {town}, calling for soviets of workers and the seizure of the factories. Police want warrants; the workers want bread.

options.label: Address the grievances
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · grievance −12 · a reformist deed

title: The Show Trials
speaker: press
body: The prisoners of the raids are due in court. {speaker} says the evidence is thin, foreign papers are watching, and the public wants a verdict.

options.label: Proceed with the trials
options.tooltip: War support +3 · legitimacy −5 · a second crackdown

title: Men in Uniform Shirts
speaker: defence
body: {speaker} reports that a league of uniformed veterans marches nightly through {town}, beating strikers and promising national rebirth. Some officers cheer them.

options.label: Ban the leagues
options.tooltip: Grievance +4 · legitimacy +3 · a crackdown on the far right

options.label: Tolerate them
options.tooltip: War support +6 · legitimacy −4 · they will not stay quiet

title: The March on the Capital
speaker: defence
body: The leagues have announced a march on the capital. {speaker} says the garrison will obey orders — if orders are given.

title: The Wireless
speaker: press
body: {speaker} says wireless sets are appearing in every parlour of {state}. Someone must decide who owns the airwaves before the private stations do.

title: A Run on the Banks
speaker: treasury
body: {speaker} reports lines of depositors outside the banks of {town}. Three savings houses are already closed, and rumour is faster than telegraph.

title: The Ration Books
speaker: treasury
body: {speaker} says shelves are emptying and prices climb weekly. The ministry proposes ration books for sugar, fat and cloth. The black market is already flourishing.

title: Rebuilding the Towns
speaker: interior
body: {speaker} presents plans to rebuild {town} and the ruined districts. Housing, rail or heavy industry — there is not money for all three.

options.label: Housing first
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.5 months of GDP · satisfaction +8 · grievance −8

options.label: Heavy industry first
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.4 months of GDP · confidence +8 · satisfaction −2

options.label: Seek foreign reconstruction loans
options.tooltip: Treasury +0.8 months of GDP · relations with our best friend +6 · confidence −3

title: The Displaced
speaker: interior
body: Columns of displaced families reach {town} with whatever they could carry. {speaker} says camps are full and local feeling is mixed.

options.label: Resettle them
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · satisfaction −3 · a humane deed

title: The Independence Petition
speaker: foreign
body: {speaker} carries a petition signed by tens of thousands in {town}, demanding self-rule. Colonial administrators elsewhere are watching what we do.

options.label: Grant self-government
options.tooltip: Grievance −15 · legitimacy +4 · relations −4 with everyone · a concession

title: Terms of Independence
speaker: foreign
body: The new assembly asks for treaty terms: a defence pact, trade preference, and a seat in the councils. {speaker} advises generosity.

options.label: Sign a friendship treaty
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.2 months of GDP · relations +5 with everyone · treaty signed

options.label: Withdraw and wish them well
options.tooltip: Nothing spent · a lost territory in the ledger

title: The Shadow of the Bomb
speaker: defence
body: {speaker} says {rival} has tested an atomic device. Schoolchildren drill under their desks and letters arrive at the ministry demanding shelters.

options.label: Build civil shelters
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.4 months of GDP · satisfaction +4 · war support +4

options.label: Call for disarmament talks
options.tooltip: Political capital −1 · relations +6 with everyone · peacemaker

title: The Television Age
speaker: press
body: {speaker} reports that television has arrived in the living rooms of {town}. A candidate's smile now counts for more than his platform.

title: The Race to the Moon
speaker: science
body: {speaker} says {rival} has put a satellite into orbit. The ministry begs for a rocket programme, and the public asks why we are not first.

options.label: Fund a space programme
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.7 months of GDP · confidence +6 · legitimacy +3

options.label: Join a joint venture with {friend}
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · relations with our best friend +8

title: Spin-offs and Spectacle
speaker: science
body: The programme has reached orbit. {speaker} says the spin-off industries are ready — if we back them — and the world is watching the launch.

options.label: Stage a grand launch
options.tooltip: Legitimacy +6 · satisfaction +4 · treasury −0.2 months of GDP

title: The Oil Embargo
speaker: treasury
body: {speaker} says petrol has tripled in price overnight. Motorists queue in {town}, hauliers threaten to block the highways, and the budget is buckling.

options.label: Subsidise fuel
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.6 months of GDP · satisfaction +5 · confidence −4

title: Odd-Even Days
speaker: interior
body: The rationing schemes have bred fraud and a thriving trade in forged coupons. {speaker} asks whether to police it or relax the limits.

title: The Open Letter
speaker: press
body: {speaker} holds a typed manifesto signed by two hundred writers and engineers, calling for an end to censorship. Copies are circulating hand to hand in {town}.

title: The Trial of the Signatories
speaker: foreign
body: The trial of the signatories has drawn foreign journalists. {speaker} says {friend} is prepared to break off talks if the sentences are harsh.

options.label: Pardon them
options.tooltip: Legitimacy −2 · relations +6 with everyone · press freedom

title: The Arms Race Bill
speaker: defence
body: {speaker} presents an estimate for new missiles and tanks. {rivalLeader} has just unveiled a larger programme, and the general staff calls it a race we cannot skip.

options.label: Match them
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.7 months of GDP · war support +8 · relations with them −5

options.label: Build a minimum deterrent
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · war support +3

options.label: Seek an arms-control treaty
options.tooltip: Political capital −1 · relations with them +8 · treaty signed

title: Flowers and Barricades
speaker: people
body: Students fill the squares of {town}, demanding peace, freedom and a say in their universities. Their elders are outraged. The police are waiting for a signal.

options.label: Open the universities to reform
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.2 months of GDP · grievance −10 · legitimacy +3

options.label: Wait for the term to end

title: The Dot-Com Boom
speaker: treasury
body: {speaker} says start-ups with no profits are valued in billions and every dentist trades shares. Analysts call it a new economy. {speaker} is less sure.

options.label: Ride the boom
options.tooltip: Confidence +8 · satisfaction +3 · a bust may follow

options.label: Cool the market with rates
options.tooltip: Confidence −3 · satisfaction −2 · treasury +0.2 months of GDP

title: The Factories Leave
speaker: interior
body: {speaker} reports that manufacturers are moving production overseas. The mill in {town} closes on Friday, and its workers are asking what the government will do.

options.label: Subsidise retraining
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.4 months of GDP · grievance −8 · a reformist deed

options.label: Impose tariffs
options.tooltip: Satisfaction +4 · confidence −5 · relations −4 with everyone · a sanction

title: The Hollowed Towns
speaker: interior
body: Years on, the retrained workers found few new jobs at home. {speaker} says the empty streets of {town} are feeding the opposition.

options.label: Fund regional investment zones
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.5 months of GDP · grievance −10 · satisfaction +4

title: The Plot Foiled
speaker: interior
body: {speaker} says a bomb plot in {town} has been foiled by luck, not design. Papers demand sweeping new powers of surveillance and detention.

options.label: Targeted policing only
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.2 months of GDP · satisfaction +1 · press freedom

options.label: Blame a foreign sponsor
options.tooltip: War support +6 · relations with them −8 · an accusation of aggression

title: The Leaked Files
speaker: press
body: A contractor has leaked the archives of the surveillance programme. {speaker} says half the capital finds it outrageous, and the other half is not sure it minds.

title: The Great Unwinding
speaker: treasury
body: {speaker} says a mortgage bank has collapsed and the others refuse to lend to each other. Panic is spreading faster than any ministry can answer.

options.label: Bail out the banks
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.8 months of GDP · confidence +10 · grievance +6

options.label: Protect households
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.6 months of GDP · satisfaction +6 · confidence −4

title: Bonuses for the Bailed Out
speaker: press
body: {speaker} reveals that the rescued banks paid record bonuses. Crowds gather outside the exchange in {town}.

options.label: Tax the bonuses
options.tooltip: Treasury +0.4 months of GDP · confidence −3 · legitimacy +4

title: The Network Arrives
speaker: science
body: {speaker} says universities are linking their computers and businesses want to follow. It could be the next telegraph, or the next headache.

options.label: Lay a national backbone
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.5 months of GDP · confidence +7 · satisfaction +3

options.label: Filter what the public may see

title: Trending in {town}
speaker: press
body: {speaker} says a video from {town} has been seen twelve million times. Hashtags demand resignations and the opposition is already quoting it.

title: Climate Refugees
speaker: interior
body: Drought and floods abroad send thousands toward {town}. {speaker} says shelters are full and {rivalLeader} warns against a 'flood of migrants' at their frontier.

options.label: Open resettlement corridors
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.4 months of GDP · satisfaction −3 · a humane deed · relations +4 with everyone

options.label: Fund camps abroad
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · relations +3 with everyone

title: The Robot Dividend
speaker: interior
body: {speaker} reports that autonomous fleets and warehouse robots have cut thousands of jobs in {town}. Firms report record profits; the unemployed report to the ministry.

options.label: Tax robots and pay a dividend
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.4 months of GDP · satisfaction +6 · grievance −10 · confidence −4

options.label: Fund retraining
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · grievance −5 · satisfaction +2

title: The Dividend Debate
speaker: treasury
body: The robot dividend is popular but costly. {speaker} asks whether to expand it into a universal income or trim it before the treasury bleeds.

options.label: Expand to universal income
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.6 months of GDP · satisfaction +8 · grievance −10

options.label: Trim it
options.tooltip: Treasury +0.3 months of GDP · satisfaction −5 · grievance +6

title: The Machine Advisers
speaker: science
body: {speaker} proposes letting an AI system draft the budget and triage the tax-office backlog. Results in pilot ministries elsewhere are impressive, and opaque.

options.label: Adopt it across ministries
options.tooltip: Treasury +0.5 months of GDP · confidence +5 · legitimacy −3

title: The Opaque Ledger
speaker: press
body: {speaker} reports that a benefits algorithm has wrongly denied thousands of claimants in {town}. No official can explain how it decided.

options.label: Mandate audits and appeals
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.2 months of GDP · legitimacy +5 · grievance −6

title: The Sea Wall
speaker: interior
body: {speaker} says storm surges are breaching the lower quarters of {town}. Engineers propose a sea wall; economists propose retreat.

options.label: Build the sea wall
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.9 months of GDP · satisfaction +5 · confidence +4

options.label: Managed retreat
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.4 months of GDP · satisfaction −4 · grievance +5

title: The Aerosol Proposal
speaker: science
body: {speaker} says stratospheric aerosols could cool the planet within a few years. It would be unilateral, cheap and irreversible. {rivalLeader} has threatened to treat it as an act of war.

options.label: Launch the aerosol fleet
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.5 months of GDP · confidence +6 · relations −10 with everyone · an act of aggression

options.label: Propose a global treaty
options.tooltip: Political capital −2 · relations +6 with everyone · treaty signed

title: Failed Monsoons
speaker: foreign
body: The aerosols have cooled the globe, but monsoons have failed in distant lands. {speaker} says {rival} is demanding compensation.

options.label: Pay reparations
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.6 months of GDP · relations with them +12 · humane deed

options.label: Deny responsibility
options.tooltip: Relations with them −12 · legitimacy −3 · an act of aggression

title: The Forged Broadcast
speaker: press
body: {speaker} says a perfect video of the opposition leader confessing to bribery is spreading. It looks real, and it is fake. Voting is in three weeks.

options.label: Mandate content verification
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.2 months of GDP · legitimacy +2 · censorship charges

title: The Heat Dome
speaker: interior
body: Fifty degrees in {town} for nine days. {speaker} reports overwhelmed hospitals and power grids on the brink of failure.

options.label: Emergency cooling centres
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · satisfaction +4 · a humane deed
